headline: Trump allies (Witkoff, Kushner) reportedly floated Europe resuming Russian gas purchases as a Ukraine peace incentive
dek: White House envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukrainian and European officials in Miami earlier this month and reportedly floated resuming Europe's purchases of Russian natural gas as part of a peace deal: transit fees for Ukraine via Ukrainian pipelines, lower energy prices for Europe.…
sources: New York Times reporting (via ChosunBiz Oct 18); White House statement to NYT
fault_line: Buy Russian gas to end the war — pragmatic peace move, or paying Moscow to keep fighting?

sections.what_happened: White House envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukrainian and European officials in Miami earlier this month and reportedly floated resuming Europe's purchases of Russian natural gas as part of a peace deal: transit fees for Ukraine via Ukrainian pipelines, lower energy prices for Europe. The European delegation was reportedly taken aback. The White House told the NYT it is 'working closely with Ukraine and European partners on a comprehensive peace plan that includes economic incentives for both Russia and Ukraine' — goal 'not simply to end the fighting but to create conditions for lasting peace.'
sections.what_verified: ChosunBiz relay of NYT; the White House statement is confirmed. No direct European-government confirmation of the gas proposal in-window.
sections.what_disputed: Europe has spent years cutting Russian-gas dependence; buying again hands Moscow export revenue and leverage — the NYT's own European sources describe dismay. A proposal is not a policy.
sections.why_matters: Washington asks Europe to fund the pipeline it sanctioned: the pocketbook-vs-peace debate, pure playbook Tier-1 energy debate bait. Numbers on screen: pre-war European gas dependence, transit-fee economics, who's taken aback.
sections.context: Background: Trump allies (Witkoff, Kushner) reportedly floated Europe resuming Russian gas purchases as a Ukraine peace incentive; NYT Oct 17
